stories.headline: OpenTelemetry in the GitHub Copilot app
stories.what_changed: GitHub added OpenTelemetry configuration for the GitHub Copilot app through enterprise-managed settings, allowing administrators to export agent activity to compatible monitoring tools.
stories.why_it_matters: Enterprise teams can follow model and tool activity through an agent session, inspect step-by-step traces when behavior is unexpected, and apply the monitoring configuration centrally.
stories.rationale: Pilot export from a limited group to a secured existing OpenTelemetry backend, validate trace usefulness and access controls, and keep prompt and response capture disabled unless a reviewed need justifies enabling it.

stories.headline: Security improvements for SSH
stories.what_changed: GitHub announced removal of RSA/SHA-1 SSH signatures and diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256, a 3072-bit minimum for newly uploaded RSA keys after October 14, 2026, and support for ML-KEM hybrid key exchange on most GitHub cloud SSH sessions.
stories.why_it_matters: Older Git clients, embedded SSH libraries, build servers, or automation can lose Git-over-SSH connectivity during brownouts and eventual removal if they still negotiate the retired algorithms.
stories.rationale: Inventory Git-over-SSH clients before the November 4 and December 9 brownouts. Confirm RSA uses SHA-2 or move new keys to Ed25519; upgrade clients that lack modern signature and key-exchange support. Ignore this item if every relevant remote uses HTTPS.

stories.headline: Deprecation notice: All-platform CodeQL bundle
stories.what_changed: GitHub deprecated the combined all-platform CodeQL bundle starting with CodeQL CLI 2.27.0 and says it will remove the bundle in mid-March 2027.
stories.why_it_matters: Bootstrap scripts, offline mirrors, CI images, or internal installers that hard-code the combined archive names must select an operating-system and architecture-specific artifact instead.
stories.rationale: Search automation for codeql-bundle.tar.gz and codeql-bundle.tar.zst, make platform and architecture selection explicit, and test replacement artifacts before March 2027.

narration:
Good morning. Today’s developer brief has three changes worth your attention: enterprise observability for the GitHub Copilot app, a GitHub SSH transition that can break older automation, and a CodeQL packaging deprecation. The first is useful now for teams operating coding agents. The other two are maintenance work with long lead times, not emergencies.

Start with the GitHub Copilot app. GitHub has added OpenTelemetry configuration through enterprise-managed settings. An administrator can configure the telemetry property in managed-settings dot J-S-O-N, choose an endpoint, and send agent activity into a compatible monitoring system.

The useful part is not simply that another product exports telemetry. It is the level of the workflow that becomes visible. GitHub says teams can follow the flow of an agent session, including requests to models and the tools the agent uses. They can inspect step-by-step execution when behavior is unexpected, and they can apply the monitoring configuration centrally instead of asking every developer to set it up.

This matters for organizations moving from chat assistance to delegated work. When an agent takes several steps, a final answer does not explain why it chose a tool, where a session slowed down, or which part of the chain failed. A trace gives operators a shared record to investigate. It also makes agent monitoring fit existing observability practice rather than creating a separate debugging island for A-I tools.

The audience is enterprise administrators, platform teams, and engineering leaders using the GitHub Copilot app. Individual developers without control of enterprise-managed settings do not have an immediate action from this announcement.

For eligible teams, the action is to run a limited rollout rather than enabling broad content capture by habit. Point a test group at a secured OpenTelemetry endpoint, confirm that session traces are useful in the monitoring tool you already operate, and decide who is allowed to view them. GitHub says prompt and response content is excluded by default. Keep that default unless there is a reviewed reason to change it, and inspect the content-capture settings before deployment. Observability data can improve diagnosis, but expanding captured content also expands the privacy and code-handling questions you must govern.

The caveat is scope. The fresh announcement establishes support in the GitHub Copilot app through enterprise settings. It does not prove that the traces answer every reliability question, and it does not provide a measured reduction in failures or debugging time. Treat this as a new operational surface to evaluate, not as evidence that agent observability is solved.

Second, GitHub announced an SSH security transition. It plans to remove the S-S-H R-S-A signature type that uses S-H-A one, remove the Diffie-Hellman group-exchange S-H-A two-fifty-six key exchange, require newly uploaded R-S-A keys to be at least three thousand seventy-two bits after October fourteenth, and add the M-L-KEM hybrid key exchange for most GitHub cloud S-S-H sessions.

The practical risk is compatibility. Old Git clients, embedded S-S-H libraries, build servers, or long-lived automation may still negotiate the algorithms GitHub is retiring. GitHub lists brownouts on November fourth and December ninth. Those are the useful deadlines for testing because a brownout can reveal a hidden dependency before permanent removal.

There are three important limits to keep intact. First, H-T-T-P-S remotes are unaffected. If every relevant remote begins with H-T-T-P-S, you can ignore this story. Second, an existing R-S-A key does not automatically need replacement. GitHub says the same key can continue when the client signs with R-S-A S-H-A two, and most compatible implementations choose that automatically. The confusing point is that the R-S-A key type and the identically named legacy S-S-H R-S-A signature are not the same thing. Third, GitHub’s schedule currently says permanent removal is January thirteenth, twenty twenty-six, even though the listed brownouts occur later in twenty twenty-six. That year is internally inconsistent. Do not plan around the stated final-removal date until GitHub corrects or clarifies it.

The action is straightforward. Inventory systems that connect to GitHub over S-S-H, especially C-I servers and Java integrations. Confirm they support R-S-A with S-H-A two and a modern key exchange. Upgrade old clients where possible. For new keys, GitHub recommends Ed two-five-five-one-nine when compatibility allows. If another service requires R-S-A, generate at least a three-thousand-seventy-two-bit key. Do not rotate working keys merely because you saw the phrase S-S-H R-S-A; verify the negotiated signature first.

Finally, CodeQL C-L-I version two point twenty-seven marks the combined all-platform bundle as deprecated. GitHub says it will remove the combined bundle in mid-March twenty twenty-seven and directs users to operating-system and architecture-specific downloads. Linux A-R-M sixty-four is already available only as a platform-specific download.

This affects maintainers who download or redistribute CodeQL directly: bootstrap scripts, offline mirrors, C-I images, and internal installers that hard-code codeql-bundle dot tar dot G-Z or codeql-bundle dot tar dot Z-S-T. Search that automation now and make platform and architecture selection explicit. Test the replacement artifact in every environment you actually support, then update checksums and cache keys as part of the same controlled change.

The caveat is important: this is a packaging deprecation, not a retirement of CodeQL analysis. Teams using managed code scanning without directly handling these bundles may have nothing to change. The removal is months away, so schedule the migration with normal maintenance rather than interrupting current work.

That is the brief. Evaluate Copilot OpenTelemetry with privacy defaults intact. Test Git-over-S-S-H before the announced brownouts, while treating GitHub’s final date as unresolved. And migrate direct CodeQL installers to platform-specific bundles before March. Everything else in the bounded scan was either older than the daily window, unsupported by useful evaluation, or too thin to justify your time today.
